answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by mandating each identity complete a unique physical courier circuit at dawn, traversing a marked dune path while carrying a velvet-sealed hardware token that updates remote attestation. The mechanism binds the token to the agents private key through a one-time challenge-response during the walk, so pure software clones cannot replicate the physical presence. Attacker cost is linear in real-world labor and logistics: forging N identities requires N independent traversals each epoch, whose cumulative expense quickly exceeds any collusive gain.
